high_level_description: A wordless documentary gouache illustration of a Versailles osmothécaire choosing one fragrance from a climate-controlled conservatory, placing one scented paper blotter into a clear sleeve for dispatch while the original bottle and thousands of preserved perfumes remain in the archive.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A windowless fragrance conservation room in Versailles with pale gray plaster walls, a sealed light-stone floor, a plain white ceiling, and cool neutral illumination. The room contains no public counter, decorative showroom, shop window, partition, niche, safe, padlock, barrier, sign, caption, letter, numeral, logo, barcode, arrow, diagram, scent trail, interface, national symbol, religious emblem.

elements.desc: Two tall temperature-controlled wine cabinets used as perfume conservation storage, with plain glass doors and deep orderly rows of small smoky glass bottles behind them. Every bottle has a simple ground-glass stopper and an unreadable blank cream inventory tab; no bottle leaves the cabinets except the single selected source on the worktable.

Adult Versailles osmothécaire perfumer at the worktable, medium-brown skin, short black curls, cream laboratory coat over a slate-blue shirt, dark trousers, and a neutral focused expression. She uses both hands to slide one plain white scent blotter into one transparent cellophane sleeve, performing an ordinary conservation and transmission gesture, never guarding the collection and never judging its contents.

Plain stainless-steel conservation worktable with a spotless light-gray top, low raised rim, simple tubular legs, and one undecorated wooden chair tucked beneath. Its broad surface separates the single selected bottle on the left from the outgoing sleeve on the right, without compartments, symbolic controls, retail packaging, mail labels, display plinths, diagrams, explanatory props.

Single selected conservation bottle resting on the left side of the worktable, small cylindrical smoky glass, plain ground-glass stopper, and pale amber liquid still filling most of the vessel. The original remains beside the archive cabinets with no visible lettering, brand, decorative cap, spray nozzle, price tag, chain, padlock, presentation box, ingredient list, formula sheet.

Transparent cellophane sleeve held above the right side of the worktable, containing exactly one narrow white paper scent blotter with only its dipped tip slightly translucent. The sleeve contains no liquid vial, formula, ingredient sample, second strip, printed character, decorative emblem, barcode, address, postage stamp, closure lock, explanatory symbol, representation of the entire collection.
